classification.difficultyReason: Interpret matching marks and overall dimensions, recover missing component heights, and recognise that two pyramids with a common base can use their combined height when separate heights are unavailable.

content.prompt: Calculate the volume of these composite solids. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Cone above a cylinder; common circular base, marked bottom centre and curved radius pointer. Ordinary outlines and hidden boundaries use house black.
spec.mathematics: Cone height 6 m, cylinder height 8 m, common radius 3 m.

spec.description: Square pyramid on a cube, with three matching double ticks and a highlighted perpendicular pyramid height.
spec.mathematics: Cube edges 6 cm; pyramid height 5 cm.

spec.description: Rectangular pyramid on a rectangular prism. The right dimension spans the total height, not the pyramid alone.
spec.mathematics: Base 6 m by 3 m; prism height 2 m; total height 4 m.

spec.description: Left-pointing cone joined to a square prism face; the circle spans that face vertically. Double ticks identify equal square-face sides. Overall length includes prism thickness.
spec.mathematics: Square side 4.8 mm, prism thickness 1.5 mm, overall axial length 5.2 mm.

spec.description: Two square-based pyramids joined at their base; matching double ticks retain the equal-edge information. Hidden rear boundaries are dashed.
spec.mathematics: Common square side and marked sloping edges 2.8 m; total apex-to-apex height 3.96 m.

answer.worked:
The matching marks give a common square base of side $2.8\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=(2.8)^2=7.84\text{ m}^2\\V_{\mathrm{tot}}&=\frac13Ah_1+\frac13Ah_2\\V_{\mathrm{tot}}&=\frac13(7.84)(3.96)\\V_{\mathrm{tot}}&\approx10.35\text{ m}^3\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Two opposed cones share a circular base. The radius pointer targets the upper-rim-to-centre segment. The apexes are not joined by an invented line.
spec.mathematics: Common radius 2.6 m; overall length 10 m; right cone height 7.1 m.
